title: Masked Autoencoder (MAE)
reading: The slide presents the Masked Autoencoder architecture as a single annotated pipeline figure, running from a randomly masked image of a flamingo, through a Transformer encoder over visible patches, to a decoder that fills in masked positions and a reconstruction compared against the original image. Stage captions along the bottom label each step of the process.

visuals.description: Left-to-right pipeline: a 5x5 patch grid of a flamingo photo with most patches greyed out ('Random masking'); the surviving visible patches stacked into a column feeding a rounded 'encoder' box ('Encode visible patches with Transformer'); the encoder's teal token column interleaved with grey mask tokens ('Expand with "mask tokens"'); a 'decoder' box producing a red token column ('Predict unknown'); and finally the reconstructed patch-grid flamingo image ('Computer L2 loss in pixels').
visuals.assertion: MAE encodes only the small visible subset of patches with a Transformer, then re-inserts learned mask tokens before a lightweight decoder reconstructs the full image, with training loss computed as L2 error in pixel space.

concepts.name: Masked Autoencoder (MAE)
concepts.why_it_matters: Self-supervised pretraining method for vision Transformers based on reconstructing masked image patches.

concepts.name: Mask tokens
concepts.why_it_matters: Placeholders inserted at masked positions so the decoder knows where to predict.

concepts.name: Pixel-space L2 reconstruction loss
concepts.why_it_matters: Defines the training signal without needing labels.

concepts.name: Vision Transformer patch tokenization
concepts.why_it_matters: The patch grid and token columns presuppose ViT-style image tokenization.
